_comment: GENERATED ONCE on 2026-09-12 and NOT regenerated. Phase 7.7 step 1.
The 'before' half of a comparison: regenerating it on a later corpus would compare that
corpus with itself, which is the mistake resolution_snapshot_v0_7_1.json exists to avoid.
search_today            -- whole-word matching over LABELS only, what search() returns now.
exact_today             -- of those, how many pass exact_matches; 1 resolves, 0 and 2 refuse.
candidates_with_aliases -- what whole-word matching over labels AND aliases would reach,
which is what step 2 opens up and step 3 turns into offers.
The alias block records the facts step 2's rules are sized against. Note that the same
collision question gives 27 under normalise and 32 under label_key: search uses the first
and exact_matches the second, so an alias index must state which it means.
non_latin_script counts aliases with a letter outside the Latin script (28). The phase
IMPLEMENTATION doc's section 2 says 54 'contain non-Latin characters'; that figure does not
reproduce under any reading tried on 2026-09-12 -- non-ASCII is 518, non-Latin script 28,
non-alphanumerics surviving normalise 47. The measured values are recorded here and the
doc's as-built section records the discrepancy. D5's one-character rule is unaffected:
two_chars_or_fewer is 19, which the doc states and which does reproduce.
collision_resolutions pins what each of the 37 colliding aliases resolves to TODAY, including
the four that resolve to nothing. Pinned per alias because 'resolved is None' must not be an
escape hatch: breaking exact_matches to compare aliases makes most of these ambiguous rather
than wrong, and a guard that skips None passes that break.
